name: Earhart
quote: A signal from the far reaches of heaven.

voices.label: Good Morning
voices.text: Let's do a preflight check of the plane's hydraulics and oil systems while it's still cool in the morning.

voices.label: Good Afternoon
voices.text: Soaring in the sky is an effective way of relieving fatigue.

voices.label: Good Evening
voices.text: Every decent pilot has experienced flying unforgettable and slightly dangerous nights once or twice. The same goes for me.

voices.label: Good Night
voices.text: Turn in already, or hypoxia is no fun the next morning, you know?

voices.label: Main Interface Voice 1
voices.text: The appeal of traditional piston aircraft lies in the simple, rigid, but intimate feel of the machine. That's something that cannot be found on any modern jets.

voices.label: Main Interface Voice 2
voices.text:
Who drank all the antifreeze from the plane?
It wasn't you, was it? You can't chug this like vodka.

voices.label: Main Interface Voice 3
voices.text: Are they asleep?

voices.label: Home Screen 5
voices.text: Wanna go on a flight, Professor? Let's fly to another sector.

voices.label: Interactive Voice 1
voices.text: Haha...

voices.label: Interactive Voice 2
voices.text: Is something giving you a hard time?

voices.label: Interactive Voice 3
voices.text: Please leave me alone.

voices.label: On Duty
voices.text: Roger.

voices.label: Obtain
voices.text: Earhart, professional pilot who loves the sky, reporting for duty! Professor, how many miles are we from our destination?

voices.label: Potential Breakthrough
voices.text: Humph, that felt awesome!

voices.label: Neural Expansion
voices.text: Air pressure, water pressure, fuel pressure, all normal. Actuators fully operational. To the horizon and beyond!

voices.label: Max Rank
voices.text: Someday, I will fly beyond the reach of light with my beloved plane!

voices.label: Join Team
voices.text: Earhart, prepped and ready!

voices.label: Battle Start
voices.text: To the horizon!

voices.label: Ultimate Skill
voices.text: Warning! Strong turbulence ahead!

voices.label: MVP 1
voices.text: Mission accomplished!

voices.label: MVP 2
voices.text: Oooh, pretty decent outcome.

voices.label: Defeat
voices.text: I can't stop...

voices.label: Oath
voices.text:
An oath? Is that something like an employment contract? Or...
Well, it makes no difference! From now on, I'll be your personal pilot! Let's make for the stars together!

voices.label: New Year
voices.text:
In some places, they organize special flybys over cities on New Year's Day, leaving behind trails of colored smoke.
I've done something like that before, but it was really tiring.

voices.label: Valentine's Day
voices.text: When flying long-haul, you should always prepare some emergency rations. Chocolate bars are a good choice. Here, like this kind. The packaging is really drab, but it's sweet as hell! There're also nuts, marshmallows, and caramel inside.

voices.label: Tanabata
voices.text: This is quite dangerous, but have you ever wondered what it'd be like to watch the Tanabata fireworks on a plane? This angle may give you an entirely different experience, haha!

voices.label: Halloween
voices.text: I hear that witches sometimes fly on their broomsticks on Halloween. So I can catch up with them if I fly a plane, right? Then what are you waiting for? Let's go!

voices.label: Christmas
voices.text:
Ugh... that was exhausting! I spent three days and three nights giving the plane a new paint job.
To celebrate Christmas, I've specially painted it red, green, and silver. I even sprayed on some edelweiss patterns. Very festive, don't you think?

voices.label: Birthday Wish
voices.text:
This is a present I prepared specially for you—a model of a red Fokker D.VII!
In the Word War just over a century ago, an ace pilot flew it and created a new milestone in human history.

voices.label: Neural Cloud
voices.text: Neural Cloud

voices.label: Intimacy 1
voices.text:
Why does the antifreeze in the hanger always go missing inexplicably?
There are rumors that some drunken ground staff chug it like vodka, but Dolls won't do that, right? Don't tell me... Hmm, the Professor doesn't strike me as someone who'd do that either.
In any case, I must catch the culprit!

voices.label: Intimacy 2
voices.text:
I can pilot a plane over a thousand kilometers and reach my destination without satellite navigation. All I have in the way of aid is a compass and a barometer.
Delivering desperately needed supplies to those who are waiting for help gives me a sense of mental and spiritual transcendence.

voices.label: Intimacy 3
voices.text:
Preparation has to be extremely thorough before every flight mission.
After all, even Dolls can't achieve 100% accuracy or safety. Even the smallest oversight could turn into a fatal mistake.
Hm... I also make mistakes every now and then, but I haven't run into any serious problems so far. I guess I'm just lucky?

voices.label: Intimacy 4
voices.text:
From steel planes to biplanes, then to monoplanes, jetliners, and UAVs... Airplanes were first invented to carry humanity's dream of flight, to "soar through the sky freely as birds".
But nowadays, aircraft can pretty much fly independently without a pilot. Even when a pilot is necessary, the job has been gradually delegated to Dolls instead...
So haven't humans lost sight of their original goal and purpose of inventing planes in the first place?

voices.label: Intimacy 5
voices.text:
Could you keep me company today, Professor? You just have to sit in the co-pilot seat and fasten your seatbelt.
Then simply kick back and enjoy the glorious view.
If you have a preference in music, feel free to bring it onboard~

career:
E-Pilots are Dolls created by Svarog Heavy Industries in response to the needs of the aviation industry in the aftermath of World War 3, which left the global satellite network paralyzed.

Compared to traditional pilots, E-Pilots not only have knowledge on how to operate various types of aircraft without requiring additional training, but they can also access the post-WW3 aviation network platform created by Svarog Heavy Industries in collaboration with all the major aviation companies. Using this encrypted information platform, they are able to complete flight tasks without satellites. With this unique advantage, E-Pilots quickly became the favorite of major airlines.

Earhart is the longest actively serving E-Pilot. She is also the only Doll with actual experience piloting all types of aircraft, and has participated in two top-secret aircraft simulation studies. With all this to her name, she was invited to join Project Neural Cloud.
infoStories:
The one great difference that separates E-Pilots, which is a Doll who operates aircraft, from other Dolls is that they cannot immediately go into service after awakening. They must undertake half a year of training before they are fully certified to fly.

As a result, these Dolls take part in a system that is not dissimilar to human schooling. As these training centers are not identical either, they also exhibit varied development.

After leaving the factory, the vast majority of Dolls are transferred to major aviation companies for basic training. After their certification, they will start a straightforward career in air shipping. Few are like Earhart, who received training at Svarog Heavy Industries, before being assigned a job.

Earhart's training experience was quite a bit different from other E-Pilots. Within just one month, Earhart far surpassed the normal results of the program. In her hands, all flying machines were as simple to operate as children's toys. After just one or two test flights, she was able to perform even the most complex of maneuvers.

Due to her outstanding performance, Earhart was assigned to a secret project in Svarog Heavy Industries—a specialized spacecraft that would rewrite the rules of the sky. When the second half of the standard training started, Earhart was conspicuously absent.

During training, Earhart neither made a single mistake, nor did she ever suffer an accident due to forces beyond her control. Despite this, she still studied all precautions written in both human and Doll flight records. She also specifically studied the procedures for dealing with extremely dangerous situations. She never really imagined that she would find herself in one, but it was always better to be safe than sorry.

As luck would so have it, during her eighth month on the job, a bird struck a weak point in the engine when she was some 300 meters off the ground. This caused the engine to sputter and stall.

She had seen how to deal with similar situations in documentaries she had watched, and she chose the most dramatic yet heroic method. Within the 40 seconds she had before she would crash, Earhart changed direction multiple times midair to avoid residential areas, and much like the hero in the documentary, she ejected at the very last moment. She was not blessed with the luck of said hero, however, and other than her core components, Earhart's entire body was torn asunder. She lost consciousness and was recovered by the logistics team that rushed over to the site of the accident.

This accident did not cause Earhart to fear flying. On the contrary, it instilled an even greater appreciation for the sky in her as she realized how vast it truly was in comparison to humans and Dolls. She also gained an even deeper respect for the heroes from the documentaries.

Since then, Earhart has gotten into the habit of making more videos. Although it made her pre-flight application procedures more complex, she wanted to record her view of the sky from the cockpit.

Later, Earhart's photography habit expanded from not only shooting the great blue yonder, to aerial photography. The first time she witnessed this novel change in perspective, she realized that it might help this era, which tended to ignore the sky, recognize the charm of flying. She applied for the use of a civilian aircraft, and on days where there were no missions, she would take the aircraft up to take photos.

After joining the Exiles, Earhart discovered that there were very few Dolls with aviation skills. As one of the few pilots capable of long-range support, Earhart had to shoulder many tasks such as support, transport, and reconnaissance.

At the same time, to complete the spacecraft test task arranged by Svarog Heavy Industries, Earhart cooperated with an insider in Project Neural Cloud to establish an independent test site outside of the Oasis. This was to prevent it from being noticed by Dolls from other enterprises.

Because there are so few Dolls doing the same work as her, the vast majority of Dolls have no way of noticing the unusual amount of time that Earhart spends on her tasks.
oathDesc: She paints a picture of the furthest reaches of the firmament for you.

projections.name: Ace Pilot
projections.desc:
Attire produced with Neural Cloud Projection upon a Doll's arrival in Magrasea. These are the clothes they are most comfortable in.
"To revive the aviation industry, we need not build more satellites. The point is to rekindle people's love of the big blue skies!"

projections.name: Azure Heavenwalker
projections.desc:
Attire and environment produced with Neural Cloud Projection upon a Doll's arrival in Magrasea, which mirrors their life in the real world.
"Earhart en route, time flown: 20 hours and 40 minutes. Report complete."

skinList.name: Wishing Projection
skinList.desc:
Warming fireworks fill the silent night, and as the embers fall, they transform into countless candleflames. This is the most beautiful scene that the Dolls left behind on a Qixi summer night.
"Still thinking back on how the sky felt? You're back on the ground, Professor! Or are you distracted because you're jelly I took the cotton candy?"

skinList.name: Starry Flight
skinList.desc:
From the "Classical Repertoire" Series — presenting the legends of film with the latest in modern technology as a tribute to milestones in movie history.
"Come, let's go see if the distant stars really do remember the childhood dreams and mirth that boring adults have forgotten."

skinList.name: Wings of Pure White
skinList.desc:
I would have us be wings of white, soaring through cloudless skies. We tire of gravity's shackles before we cross the threshold of happiness.
""Is the treasure called happiness hidden on the other side of the blue sky? Then—let us go there, upon a pair of white wings!""
